hints.junior: A CSP header went in, the console filled with 'Refused to execute inline script' — and the nav menu that used inline JS just stopped working.
hints.mid: script-src 'self' says nothing about where a script sits in the markup, only whether the browser trusts it, inline is untrusted by default.
hints.staff: This is CSP working as designed, an attacker's injected inline script would run exactly as freely as yours if inline executed by default.

hints.junior: Toggle the policy and watch which inline script runs, your own, an attacker's, both, or neither.
hints.mid: The script's text never changes, only the policy and whether the tag carries a matching nonce decide what runs.
hints.staff: The fixed state blocks the injected script for a different reason than the broken state blocks everything, discrimination by nonce is the whole point.

hints.junior: 'unsafe-inline' makes the errors stop and also reopens the exact hole CSP was added to close, don't reach for it.
hints.mid: A nonce is generated fresh per response and matched on the script tag, an attacker's payload never gets that response's nonce.
hints.staff: Nonces and hashes don't cover onclick="..." attributes without 'unsafe-hashes', moving to addEventListener is the more portable fix.

hints.junior: Ship a new policy as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first, it logs violations without blocking anything, so you can find breakage before it ships.
hints.mid: A nonce reused across requests, or hardcoded into a static file, defeats the mechanism entirely, it has to be freshly random every response.
hints.staff: A hash is computed over exact bytes, a minifier that reformats inline script differently between builds silently breaks the allowlist on every deploy.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about adding a Content Security Policy header and watching the nav menu and other inline scripts quietly stop working.
The fix is a nonce, a random value generated fresh for every response, added to the policy and matched on the script tag you actually own.
Toggle between a plain policy and a nonce based one, and watch whether your own script runs and whether an attacker's injected one does too.
Don't fix a CSP error by allowing unsafe inline scripts everywhere. Give your own inline script a nonce instead, and keep everything else blocked.
